questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

He missed the college bus / because he woke up / unpardonably lately in the morning.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**unpardonably lately**" is incorrect because "**lately**" refers to a recent time in the past and is not suitable in the context of waking up at a specific (late) time.
 
• The correct word should be "**late**," which indicates tardiness or delay in action — suitable for time-based events like waking up late.
 
• "Unpardonably late" accurately conveys the idea of being so late that it is almost unforgivable.
 
• Therefore, the adverb "**lately**" must be replaced with the adjective "**late**" to correctly complete the phrase.

Hence, the correct answer is **Option 4: unpardonably lately in the morning**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He missed the college bus because he woke up unpardonably late in the morning."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lately** means “recently” and is used for actions that happened in the near past (e.g., "I have seen him lately").
 
• **Late** refers to being delayed or not on time and is appropriate for specific moments or schedules (e.g., "He arrived late to class").

questions.question:
**The given sentence contains a grammatical error. Identify the segment that contains the error.**

If I am you, I wouldn’t take the risk of going to the market.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is** 'If I am you'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is **grammatically incorrect.**
 
• Here,** 'If I were you' **should be used instead of** 'If I am you'.**
 
• **"If I were you" **is used when we give advice by imagining ourselves in the position of the other person.
 
• The structure of such sentences is as follows:-
 
 
• If I were you + I would/wouldn't + V1 + Object.
 
 
 
• **If I were you** ... is used when giving advice about what you would do in the same situation as the other person.
 
• You imagine yourself in their position or situation and what you would do or how you would react.
 
• **For Examples:-**
 
 
• If I **were **you, I would study more.
 
• If I **were **you, I would stop doing that.
 
• If I **were **you, I would go to the doctor.
 
• If I **were **you, I wouldn't play with those wires.
 
 
 
• We can also change the order of the sentence.
 
• **For Examples:-**
 
 
• I would study more if I **were **you.
 
• I would be more careful if I **were **you.
 
• I wouldn't do that if I **were **you.
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

**Correct Sentence:__*** **If I were you**, I wouldn't take the risk of going to the market.*

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

A book market / was been operated by some readers / in the street when / they reached there.

options.text: was been operated by some readers

questions.solution:
The erroneous part is option 3) i.e. 'was been operated by some readers.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the part 'was been operated by some readers.'
 
• Let's look at the structure of passive voice in the **past continuous tense**: Object + was/were + being + past participle (V3) + (by + subject) (Passive Voice) 
 
• **Example:**
 
 
• *He told me that the things **were being arranged** by Disha.*
 
 
 
• Thus,** 'been'** should be replaced by** 'being'**.
 
• Therefore in the given sentence, we need to use 'was being operated' in place of 'was been operated' to make the sentence grammatically correct.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

 

Correct sentence:__* A book market **was being operated by some readers** in the street when they reached there.*

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

I noticed that they / did not went to / the museum but entered / a shopping complex.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the third part of the given sentence, the phrase 'did not went' is incorrect.
 
• The correct form should be 'did not go' because when using 'did' in the past tense, the base form of the verb 'go' should be used, not the past form 'went'.
 
• Therefore, the correct phrase should be 'did not go'.

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Correct sentence: *I noticed that they did not go to the museum but entered a shopping complex.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Whenever 'did' is used in a question or negative sentence in the past tense, the main verb should be in its base form.
 
• Example: She did not eat the cake. (Not: She did not ate the cake.)
 
• Similarly: Did they go to the museum? (Not: Did they went to the museum?)

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. 

It were so painful / to give up / my last hope.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is: **It were so painful**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is incorrect because the **subject-verb agreement** is incorrect.
 
• "It" is a **singular subject**, but "were" is a **plural verb**. The correct verb to use with a singular subject is "was."

Therefore, the correct sentence would be:*** It was__ so painful to give up my last hope.***

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence, which contains the grammatical error.**

Unless you do not run fast, you cannot catch the bus.
questions.solution:
Here, one should understand the usage of the conjunction ***unless***.

**Unless** means **if not**. It is used to state what will or will not happen if something else does not happen or is not true. Thus, it expresses a condition and its possible consequences.

For eg:

 
• *You can’t get a job **unless **you’ve got the required skills.*
 
• ***Unless **you work hard, you cannot pass this semester.*

 

In the same way, when **unless **is used in the sentence, we will not use **not **in the sentence.

The corrected sentence: ***Unless you run** fast, you cannot catch the bus.*

Hence, **option 1 is the correct answer.**

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

He finally / recalled that / the thieves have leave / from the front door.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: ​**the thieves have leave**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The error is related to the verb tense.
 
• In this case, the present perfect tense "**have leave**" is incorrect.
 
• The **correct form should be in the past tense**, as the action of leaving occurred before the recalling in the past.
 
• The **correct phrase** should be "**the thieves had left**."
 
• **Corrected sentence**: *He finally recalled that the thieves had left from the front door.*
 
• In this corrected sentence, the past perfect tense "**had left**" is used to indicate that the thieves left before the main action of recalling took place.

Thus, **option 1** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.**

I can’t talk right now. / I am being really busy. / I'll call you later.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error in the sentence is located in the phrase **"I am being really busy.**" 
 
• The use of **"being"** is incorrect in this context because **"busy"** is a state, not an action that is being performed. Therefore, the continuous tense is not appropriate here.
 
• The **correct form** of the phrase should be **"I am really busy.**" This **properly conveys** the speaker's state of being very busy without implying that it is an ongoing action they are actively engaging in.
 
• **"Being"** is often used with verbs in the Present Continuous tense to indicate an action that is currently happening.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is- '**Option 2'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **I can't talk right now:** This option is grammatically correct and expresses the speaker's inability to communicate at the moment due to being busy.
 
• **I'll call you later**: This part of the sentence correctly uses the future tense "I will (I'll)" to promise a return call, which makes it appropriate and grammatically correct.

questions.question:
Identify the segment in the sentence, which contains the grammatical error.

Hardly he had stepped out of the house when a tree fell on the roof.
questions.solution:
Here, one must know the** use of inversion **in these types of sentences.

Remember,

If hardly, scarcely, barely and no sooner are in the initial position, we use an inverted word order i.e the auxiliary verb goes before the subject.

For eg:

* *Scarcely had she finished reading when she fell asleep. 

In the question too, this rule should be followed i.e. it should be like:

*Hardly **had he** stepped out of the house when a tree fell on the roof.*

Hence, **option 2 is the correct answer.**

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Hardly __we had boarded__ the train when it started to move.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**had we boarded**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• If the second event occurs immediately after the first, we can express that idea using the structure: "hardly...when."
 
• In this structure hardly introduces the event that occurred first.
 
• The sentence is in past perfect tense, which requires the auxiliary verb "had".
 
• **When we begin a sentence with a negative word, we put the auxiliary verb before the subject.**
 
 
• **​Thus, "had" will be used before the subject "we."**
 
 
 
• "Hardly" is an adverb of time, indicating that the action of boarding the train happened just before another action (the train starting to move).
 
• The correct sentence structure is "Hardly had we boarded the train when it started to move."

Hence, **the correct answer is option 4**.

questions.question:
**In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.**

Mohit did not (1) went to school (2)yesterday as he (3) was unwell. (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is ***'Went to school' ***

*** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__***

__
 
• The second part of the sentence carries an error in the sentence. 
 
• The error is of *'Form of the verb'* which is wrongly used. 
 
• According to the grammatical rule, we always use** 'Did + Base form of the verb used (V1)'**. The verb that follows 'Did' as an auxiliary, is always supposed to follow the 'First form of the verb'. __
 
• According to the rule, the sentence will *not have 'went'* (as the V2 but will have 'V1)
 
• 'Mohit did not went to school yesterday as he was unwell.
 
• Thus and so, the correct sentence will be: __*Mohit did not go to school yesterday as he was unwell.*__

questions.question:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

Vini bought two new dresses but either is suitable for the festival.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4 i.e. either is.

 
• The error is in the third segment of the sentence and it has to be modified.
 
• Notice the **conjunction ‘but’** used in the middle of the sentence. It is **used to introduce a phrase or clause contrasting** with what has already been mentioned.
 
 
• Hence the sentence would mean: Although Vini bought two new dresses, both of them are not suitable to be worn for the festival. 
 
 
 
• The pronoun ‘either’ used in the sentence is incorrect. It means ‘one or the other of two people or things’.
 
• It has to be replaced with ‘neither’. Neither means "not the one and not the other" or "not either." 
 
 
• The following example shows this use: *You can wear **neither** of the dresses to the party* (you cannot wear the one dress, you cannot wear the other dress also).
 
 

Hence the phrase “either is” should be replaced with “neither of them is”.

Correct sentence: Vini bought two new dresses but neither of them is suitable for the festival.

questions.question: Select the option with the correct use of future tense.

options.text: If you had work hard in the same manner, you will soon achieve success.
If you work hard in the same manner, you will soon achieve success.
If you have work hard in the same manner, you will soon achieve success.
If you worked hard in the same manner, you will soon achieve success

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2)**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The second option correctly uses the future tense by stating, **"If you work hard in the same manner, you will soon achieve success."**
 
• It properly combines the present simple tense **"work"** with the** future simple tense "will achieve."**
 
• This structure follows the** first conditional format**, which is used for real or possible situations in the future.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

**Correct Sentence:** ***"If you work hard in the same manner, you will soon achieve success."***

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "If you had work hard in the same manner, you will soon achieve success."** – This is incorrect because "had work" is not grammatically correct; it should be "had worked" for past perfect tense, but then it doesn't match with "will achieve."
 
• **Option 3: "If you have work hard in the same manner, you will soon achieve success."** – This is incorrect because "have work" is not correct; it should be "have worked," but the present perfect tense with "will achieve" is not the correct match in this conditional sentence structure.
 
• **Option 4: "If you worked hard in the same manner, you will soon achieve success."** – This is incorrect as it mixes past simple tense "worked" with future simple tense "will achieve," which typically demands a different conditional format (second conditional).

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been divided into four parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options.**

This boy / is cleverest / of all / in the class.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **is cleverest**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the omission of the definite article "**the**" before "**cleverest**."
 
• When using **the superlative form** to indicate that someone or something has the highest degree of quality within a group, it's necessary to include the definite article "**the**."
 
• This helps specify that the individual being referred to is the most outstanding or best in comparison to all others in the group.
 
• The **corrected sentence** becomes: ***This boy is the__ cleverest of all in the class.***

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Most probably, / he come / to office / next Tuesday.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. he come .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is about a future event, so the correct form should be **"he will come"**.
 
• In English, to indicate a future event, we use the auxiliary verb **"will"** along with the base form of the main verb.
 
• The correct structure for this sentence should be **"Most probably, he will come to office next Tuesday."**.

Correct sentence: *Most probably, he **will come** to office next Tuesday*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Present Simple Tense:**

 
 
• **Structure:** Subject + base verb (he comes).
 
• **Example:** He comes to the office every day.
 
• **Usage: **Describes habitual actions.
 
 
 
• **Future Simple Tense:**
 
 
• **Structure: **Subject + will + base verb.
 
• **Example: **He will come to the office next Tuesday.
 
• **Usage: **Describes actions that will happen in the future.

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been divided into four parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options.**

The sun / revolves / around / a earth.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **a earth**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The error is in the use of the article "**a**" before "earth."
 
• Indefinite article '**A**' is used when referring to a non-specific item or an item for the first time.
 
 
• **Example**: *I saw a cat in the backyard.*
 
 
 
• Definite Article "**the**" is used when referring to a specific item that has already been mentioned or is known to both the speaker and the listener.
 
 
• **Example**: *I saw the cat in the backyard again.*
 
 
 
• When referring to our planet, "**earth**" should be preceded by the definite article "**the**" rather than the indefinite article "**a**."
 
• The definite article "**the**" is used to specify a particular item, in this case, **the Earth around** which the sun revolves.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**.

questions.question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

She was waiting for a opportunity to start her own business.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**for a opportunity**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the given sentence, the error lies in the part "for a opportunity."
 
• **The correct phrase is "for an opportunity" because "opportunity" starts with a vowel sound.**
 
• Using "a" before a word starting with a vowel sound is a common mistake in English.
 
• **We use "an" before a word starting with a vowel sound.**
 
• Thus, the correct article to use is "an" and the correct phrase is "for an opportunity."

Hence, **the correct answer is option 3**.

**Corrected sentence**: "She was waiting for **an **opportunity to start her own business."

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment in which the article has been used INCORRECTLY.

Ms. Rose is a / sweetest of / all the girls / in the class.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the second part of the given sentence, the article 'a' is incorrect.
 
• The correct usage should be **'the'** before the superlative adjective **'sweetest'**.
 
• Therefore, the corrected part should be 'the sweetest of'.

Hence, the correct statement should be: *Ms. Rose is **the sweetest of** all the girls in the class*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Articles **'a'**, **'an'**, and **'the'** are used before nouns or adjectives to specify or generalize them.
 
• Use **'the'** before superlative adjectives (e.g., *the tallest*, *the sweetest*).
 
• Use **'a'** or **'an'** before singular, countable nouns when referring to them in a general sense (e.g., *a book*, *an apple*).

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

The scooter that / I am using / these days is belonging / to my brother.
questions.solution:
The erroneous segment is **'these days is belonging'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is **not correct.**
 
• The error lies in **part 3 **of the given sentence.
 
• The error lies in **'these days is belonging'** part of the sentence.
 
• Here, Belong is a static verb and it is not to be used in **progressive sentence.**
 
• Instead of** 'is belonging'** we will use **'belongs' **in **simple present tense** for making the sentence free from any error.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **option 4.**

**Correct Sentence:**__ *The scooter that I am using these days __**belongs**__ to my brother.*

questions.question:
**Select the segment in the sentence, which contains a grammatical error.**

This furnitures has been taken on hire for the function in the college.

**In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.**

Those who follow a healthy routine is likely enjoying good health.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3.**

The error is in the 3rd part of the sentence. *'is likely enjoying'* is a wrong phrase used.

__
 
• The Subject-Verb agreement rule is violated here. The plural subject takes a plural verb.__
 
• **'Those'** is a plural subject and in accordance, the verb must be **'are'.**
 
• Also, the **to-infinitive form** must be used after *likely.*

Thus the correct sentence will be: *Those who follow a healthy routine are likely to enjoy good health.*

questions.question:

__

questions.question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

Hiking across an Himalayas is going to be a tough task for a beginner.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the use of the article "**an**" before the term "**Himalayas**."
 
• The correct article to use before a word starting with a consonant sound is "**a**."
 
• The correct phrase should be "**a Himalayas**," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
